text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- At least 40 "terrorists" have been killed by security forces still besieging more than 200 others in huge anti-terrorist operation in western province of Tissemsilt.
- Campaign for parliamentary elections hits cruising speed.
- Sixty containers of imported potatoes rot in Algiers port: equivalent of two million dinars go up in smoke.
- Islamist leader Mahfoud Nanhah tells supporters his Movement for a Peaceful Society will score well in election.
- Outbidding poll tactics push rival candidates to give voters false promises like scrapping taxes, erasing shantytowns and giving young people houses to marry and jobs for every employment-seeker.
- Government, fighting rumours over milk price rise, says there will be no increase before or after elections.
- Temperature rises to abnormal 37 degrees Celsius (99 F) in coastal city of Algiers while it was only 13 degrees (55 F) in southern city of In-Salah in desert.
- Rival candidates begin attacking each other's private lives.
- Former prime minister Redha Malek, campaigning for Republican National Alliance in western town of Relizane, says legal Algerian Islamist parties back terrorism in Algeria.
